picard: the first producer of the Jacobian datum, from a Zariski chart family

A finite family of relatively representable open immersions into the sigma-extension
sheaf of the degree-zero Picard functor, jointly Zariski-locally surjective, with
charts quasi-compact and locally of finite type over the base field, produces
JacobianData C.  The representing object is the glued scheme placed over Spec k by
the sigma-component of the universal element (pic0RepresentableByOfCharts).

The two finiteness certificates are discharged from the charts, not assumed:
locally-of-finite-type is local on the source and the glue maps of the glue data are
an open cover, and over the affine base Spec k quasi-compactness is compactness of
the glued space, supplied by finitely many compact charts.  The bridge is
toGlued_comp_gluedHom: the i-th glue map followed by the structure morphism of the
glued object is the structure morphism of the i-th chart, both being sigma-components
of the same restriction of the universal element.

Also records that the GeometricallyReduced hypothesis of Pic0SigmaSheaf is not an
extra assumption over the frozen hypothesis bundle of Challenge.lean: it is an
instance consequence of smoothness of relative dimension one.

picard: the Jacobian-datum producer for an infinitely-indexed chart atlas

JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace drops the finiteness of the index type and takes
compactness of the glued space directly.  The locally-of-finite-type certificate still
descends from the charts with no finiteness hypothesis at all, since being locally of

are indexed by divisor classes, one per class whose twisted fibre class has an effective
witness, and that index set is not finite.  Compactness of the glued object is then a
theorem about the Jacobian rather than bookkeeping.

id: AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.field-size
title: 'Field-size: over a small finite field, what is DivFamZar? — the one remaining
  human decision'
projects:

summary: "ANSWERED 2026-07-26 (run 0048 round 4). Not blocked any more, and not a\
  \ human decision after all —\nthe bound is a theorem, sharp in both directions.\
  \ Deliverable: informal/spec-dd-r.md ADDENDUM 4\n§4.4 (commit d7e8348ce). Inbox\
  \ I-0346's standing question is discharged.\n\nTHE ANSWER.  R1 -- varying the pinned\
  \ pair of P^1-points per cover member, i.e. the p1-aut ->\nfibre-avoid -> cert-relocalize\
  \ chain -- is correct IF AND ONLY IF |P^1(k)| >= n + 2, where n is\nthe degree,\
  \ pinned to the genus g by the functor.\n\nBoth directions come from one fibrewise\
  \ reduction (ADDENDUM 4 §4.2).  For c in P^1(k) let W_c be\nthe image in Spec R\
  \ of supp D meeting pi^{-1}(c); it is closed because supp D is finite over R,\n\
  and s in W_c iff the FIBRE supp(D_s) meets pi^{-1}(c).  Since D_s is finite of degree\
  \ n over\nkappa(s), its image in |P^1| has at most n closed points.\n  IF: pick\
  \ c in P^1(k) outside that image and any c' /= c; then Spec R minus W_c confines\
  \ D to the\n  chart complementary to pi^{-1}(c).  Doing this at every s gives a\
  \ Zariski cover on which the\n  divisor is confined, with the pair varying per member\
  \ -- exactly what R1 allows.\n  ONLY IF: if the sum over c in P^1(k) of e_c is at\
  \ most n, where e_c is the minimal degree of a\n  closed point of C over c, then\
  \ a divisor of the form sum_c q_c + padding lies in W_c for EVERY\n  c in P^1(k),\
  \ and no pinned pair confines it.\n\nCONSEQUENCES, and they decide the certificate\
  \ route.\n * p1-aut is NOT dead.  It is correct over every infinite field, and over\
  \ F_q whenever q >= g+1.\n * It cannot discharge the challenge on its own.  Challenge.lean:96-99\
  \ states the Jacobian over an\n   ARBITRARY field and archon-protected.yaml forbids\
  \ adding a hypothesis, so R1 must be paired\n   with descent (dat-g) or replaced.\n\
  \ * Of the three options this leaf was opened to choose between, (a) \"accept |P^1(k)|\
  \ >= n+2 as a\n   hypothesis\" is now known to be exactly the right hypothesis and\
  \ exactly what the challenge\n   forbids; (b) descent from a big enough k' is viable\
  \ and is the pairing R1 needs; (c) degree-d\n   closed points is unnecessary --\
  \ it is subsumed by R2, which is cleaner.\n * R2 is the only field-uniform fix and\
  \ is no longer a gamble: supp D is finite over R, hence\n   contained in a single\
  \ affine open of C x_k Spec R (avoidance for families, Stacks 0B8B), so a\n   cover\
  \ with one straddling piece always exists.  Generalising FinCoverData's piece type\
  \ to\n   arbitrary affine opens of the relative curve is the statement the geometry\
  \ already supports.\n\nRelated and settled the same round: the on-stratum witness\
  \ the no-go lacked now exists at g >= 2\nover any field (ADDENDUM 4 §4.3), so the\
  \ no-go is not vacuous on the campaign's stratum; and\nADDENDUM 3's shrink-stability\
  \ argument was the wrong criterion (a span-top cover cannot delete a\npoint) --\
  \ under the criterion it stated, the campaign's own genus-0 example would be evaded.\n"
